brief: Today's posts centered on AI coding agents and model launches, including a GPT-6.2 billing correction and Andrej Karpathy's Civilization-style map built from US public data. Thariq announced he has joined OpenAI from Anthropic, the most notable item beyond the product news.

themes.label: AI coding harnesses and agents
themes.summary: Builders discussed coding agents as the base for knowledge work, and harness speed, durability and skills like Frontend Slides.

themes.label: GPT-6.2 billing correction
themes.summary: OpenAI said a launch billing error discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage, and it is fixing the error and adding a banked reset.

themes.label: Gemini local voices and inbox use
themes.summary: Josh Woodward highlighted Gemini adding 66 local voices and accents and users applying it to tasks like Inbox Zero.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Wrote that coding shows how knowledge work will move from manual research and typing to coordinating agents that pursue goals.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Explained a launch billing mistake that discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage, saying the fix means users reach limits faster and adding a banked reset for paid plans.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Said their Frontend Slides skill reached 32k GitHub stars without promotion and asked why people still use it over slides from Claude or Codex. Also wrote that high-retention software is hard to build.

builders.name: Madhu Guru
builders.summary: Argued that AI native teams will push surrounding organizations to change, since faster coding does not yet raise shipped products or business impact in most companies.

builders.name: Sam Altman
builders.summary: Announced a small test of Private Inference within OpenAI Private Intelligence, aimed at business privacy. Also posted a brief reply about hyperstitioning.

builders.name: Training Data
builders.summary: Shared a podcast episode with OpenAI's Noam Brown on why game theory did not lead to general intelligence, recorded live at No Limit Finals.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Described the fx harness, which fits subagents, MCP, skills and sessions in 6mb, and announced a 10x workflow speedup. Also built lsx, a terminal file finder, with fx and DeepSeek subagents.

builders.name: Ryo Lu
builders.summary: Mostly personal posts, including a cursor kitty and a name explanation.

builders.name: Peter Steinberger
builders.summary: Criticized Google for restricting CLIs like gog while building an MCP.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary: Shared showcase posts: origami folded in code, a robot arm playing checkers, and a question about what people are exploring with Fable 5.2.

builders.name: Andrej Karpathy
builders.summary: Built a Civilization-style US map from 31 public data sources, with 7 hours and 45K lines of code using Opus 5.5, mapping GDP to gold yield and industries to districts.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Announced 66 new Gemini local voices and accents and shared user examples of tasks done with Gemini, including Inbox Zero.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Wrote about the pressures on new media founders and argued that cost per task hides model reliability problems. Also shared a short Anthropic blog link.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Announced the next guest in a weekly SF session, Stripe's Jeff Weinstein, on agent payments and commerce, and posted a coffee shop recommendation.

builders.name: Nan Yu
builders.summary: Posted short comments on chat interfaces for AI and an Apple product wish, with mostly link-only posts.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Highlighted a Nick Bostrom clip on superintelligence and shared a stat showing median startup growth of 10x with AI help.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Announced joining OpenAI from Anthropic, saying the company builds AI products for over a billion people. Other posts were personal.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Said large scale software migration is now viable when results can be verified, which matters for aging critical infrastructure.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Posted brief link-only and personal posts, including praise for a leader using Every's dot.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Posted a single link with no commentary.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Shared a desktop app project for cooking and a view that keeping humans able to follow AI actions is a major product challenge.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Posted a joke about Jensen Huang and therapy, with no substantive product or industry content.
